punchline: In Hari's telling, a Cambodian farmer's depression lifted after neighbours bought him a cow.
thirty_sec: Johann Hari tells of a Cambodian farmer who lost his left leg to a land mine and sank into despair even with an artificial limb. Doctors and neighbours sat down with him and bought him a cow so he could farm dairy. Over months and years his depression went away. Hari reads it as a lost future being rebuilt, though critics say he picks his evidence selectively.
